label: ex-the-empty-relation-and-the-empty-function
tail:
VERDICT: CLEAN

BOUNDARY:
- Empty set as relation: vacuously satisfies "every element is an ordered pair"; domain and range are empty; field is empty. No defect.
- Empty relation on every set: $\varnothing \subseteq A \times A$ holds vacuously for every set $A$ by the definition of subset. No defect.
- Empty set as the only relation on $\varnothing$: $\varnothing \times \varnothing = \varnothing$, and the only subset of $\varnothing$ is $\varnothing$. No defect.
- Empty equivalence relation on $\varnothing$: reflexivity, symmetry, and transitivity all universally quantify over the empty set, so they hold vacuously. No defect.
- Empty function $\varnothing \to B$: single-valued vacuously, domain empty, range empty $\subseteq B$; unique because any function with empty domain must be empty. No defect.
- Bijection $\varnothing \to \varnothing$: injectivity and surjectivity both vacuous over empty domain/codomain. No defect.
- Non-surjection $\varnothing \to \{\varnothing\}$: codomain nonempty, domain empty, so surjectivity fails; injectivity still vacuous. No defect.
- Empty product $\prod_{i \in \varnothing} A_i = \{\varnothing\}$: the empty function is the unique element, consistent with the definition of the indexed product. No defect.
- Both directions of L11 ($A \times B = \varnothing \iff A = \varnothing \lor B = \varnothing$): only the forward direction is used to conclude $\varnothing \times \varnothing = \varnothing$; the citation is faithful. No defect.
- Empty index set and singleton index set: empty index set handled correctly; one-element index set not used. No defect.

CHECKED: Read every numbered step (1.1 through 4.1) and compared every cited fact (L1–L15) against the full text of its declared dependency. All steps are mathematically licensed by the cited material, and no fact is inflated or misrepresented.
